1.why: All seven screens are static with no pop-ups, banners or animation, though the dark Logs panel with long hex tokens adds visual clutter that reduces overall cleanliness.

2.why: Bold headings, filled teal primary buttons and highlighted status banners stand out clearly, but the large dark Logs panel visually competes with the actual task controls.

3.why: Each step shows a single short form so the needed field is obvious, yet the recovery code must be hunted for inside a 64-character hex string in a developer Logs panel.

4.why: The 5-chip stepper and one-action-per-screen reduce memory load, but she must carry over a long code and remember composite password rules (12+ chars, upper, lower, number, symbol).

5.why: No 'Remember me' checkbox, password manager hint, autofill affordance or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: Nothing familiar is surfaced back to her — the email is not echoed at sign-in, no saved account/avatar or masked identifier is displayed.

7.why: All copy is short, plain and reassuring, e.g. 'Start when you are ready. We will guide you one step at a time.'

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the seven screenshots, so there is no observable evidence that errors name the problem and the fix.

9.why: No placeholder text, sample email or example password is provided; the password requirement is described in prose only.

10.why: The password and emailed-code paths are labelled clearly, but no alternative such as face/biometric or passkey login is offered or explained.

11.why: Every step presents one primary button (at most two on the Verify step) and a single input, avoiding simultaneous competing options.

12.why: Each screen opens with an explicit outcome banner ('Code verified…', 'Password saved…', 'Privacy statement accepted…') plus a matching log entry.

13.why: A persistent 'Need help?' link appears on all screens along with short guiding tips like 'Take your time: this step will stay here until you are ready.'

14.why: 'Send a new recovery code' allows a retry at the verify step, but no back/edit link exists to correct a mistyped email or return to a previous step.

15.why: All seven screens reuse the same header, stepper, banner, form and button layout with identical typography and colour scheme.
